transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-02-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Bluemoor), Tom Brewer (Security Lead), Rajiv Menon (Head of Infra), Sofia Cruz (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO artifacts availability, trust center access, RBAC + SSO (SAML), audit log policies and KMS integration for EU data residency scenarios. Customer is evaluating Redwood for hosting inference for PII-containing insurance claims pipeline; primary concerns are data residency, key management, and auditability.

Topics Covered:
- SOC 2 Type II reports access and redaction options
- ISO 27001 scope and mapping to Bluemoor controls
- Trust Center walkthrough and evidence handoff process
- RBAC and SSO (SAML) integration options, SCIM provisioning
- Audit logs: retention, export, log lineage (ingest -> inference -> logs)
- Encryption/KMS: BYOK, Cloud KMS vs HSM, key rotation
- Data residency and region routing / private deployment options

Questions Raised:
- Can Redwood provide host-level logs and per-token audit trails?
- How does Redwood handle customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private vs Hosted?
- What is the default retention for audit logs and can it be extended for 7 years?

Action items and next steps (see metadata for details).

--- Transcript Body (imperfect transcription, timestamps every ~40s):
[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time, um this is Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We've got Jia on the call who is our solutions engineer and Maya from customer success. How are you doing?
[00:08] Lena: Hey Samir, hi Jia, good thanks. We wanted to knock out a posture review so our security folks can feel comfortable. We have payment-adjacent PII, so data residency is a big one.
[00:17] Tom: Yeah, hi all. I will focus on SOC two and ISO areas, also KMS integration.
[00:22] Jia: Awesome, thanks. Quick agenda: I'll run through what artifacts we can share, how Trust Center access works, then we can go into RBAC/SSO and KMS specifics, and finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Rajiv: Sounds good. We're on AWS primarily, EU data centers are required for some EU customers, so curious about routing, region constraints, and whether logs ever transit the US.
[00:40] Jia: Great question, at a high level Redwood has hosting in multiple regions; for hosted customers we can ensure inference stays in region and logging - sorry logs - can be configured to land in a regional bucket. For regulated workloads we usually recommend either Dedicated capacity or Private deployment in a VPC so you control egress.
[00:56] Tom: Can you share what type of logs you retain by default? We need request traces, per-token indicators, and admin activity for audit.
[01:05] Jia: Default retention is 90 days in the hosted console for application-level logs, with the option to export to customer S3 or SIEM. We keep structured request traces, model versioning events and admin changes. The audit trail includes who triggered model rollouts, who changed routing rules, etc. Token-level logs are treated carefully — by default we store token metadata but the payloads are not preserved unless configured for debug. I should note transcription may've swapped a couple terms, but essentially we can capture per-request metadata for audits.
[01:30] Sofia: We need proof for SOC 2 that logs are immutable and tamper-evident — is there WORM or a signed log export?
[01:38] Jia: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed S3 with object lock/WORM policies and you can pipe logs to a WORM-enabled bucket. For hosted customers we can provide signed attestations and digital signatures on exported bundles, but the hosted path can't natively enforce S3 object-lock on our managed buckets.
[01:55] Samir: To add to that, we also provide a compliance package with a read-only Trust Center link and downloadable artifacts — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, penetration test summaries (redacted). We'll share the redacted SOC 2 by email.
[02:06] Lena: When you say "Trust Center link" does that give us direct access to the evidence repository or just summary reports? We need reviewer access for our auditor.
[02:13] Jia: The Trust Center can be configured per-account; for enterprise customers we set up a reviewer role with time-limited access so auditors can pull evidence. You can also request direct SSO for auditors via SAML or provide shareable signed artifacts.
[02:24] Tom: SSO — we run Okta; does Redwood support SAML 2.0 and SCIM? We want automated user provisioning and role mapping into RBAC.
[02:31] Jia: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC maps groups to roles; we can map Okta groups to admin/viewer/engineer roles. There are also API tokens scoped to teams for programmatic access. Sometimes the automatic mapping needs a little tweak during onboarding.
[02:46] Rajiv: For KMS, are you supporting BYOK with Cloud KMS (AWS KMS) and also HSM-backed keys for the private deploy? We need keys to never leave our control.
[02:55] Jia: We support BYOK in both Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted we offer customer-managed keys via partner KMS integration — e.g., we can use your AWS KMS keys in the region. For strict FIPS/HSM requirements we recommend Private on-prem or our VPC package with an HSM-backed KMS. In that setup keys are managed by your KMS/HSM and Redwood holds references only.
[03:18] Tom: Do you have flow diagrams for that? We need to show key lifecycle — generation, rotation, use in inference and destruction.
[03:25] Jia: Yes, I will send a KMS/HSM integration diagram with the typical call paths and key rotation recommendations. It includes key wrapping, envelope encryption, and how ephemeral in-memory keys are used for performance without persisting plaintext.
[03:40] Lena: Data residency: we must ensure no U.S. egress for EU customer data. Is this enforceable on hosted?
[03:47] Samir: Hosted can be region-restricted, but the guaranteed way is Dedicated in EU or Private. We can set routing policies so requests go to EU-only endpoints and fallback to other regions is disabled. We also document network flows and provide attestations for egress policies.
[03:59] Sofia: For SOC 2 we also need to map our internal controls to Redwood controls. Do you provide a control matrix?
[04:06] Jia: Yes, we have a controls mapping template that maps SOC 2 and ISO controls to Redwood features and evidence artifacts. We'll attach a pre-filled mapping and you can adjust which controls remain with Bluemoor vs those covered by Redwood.
[04:17] Tom: About log retention — we might need seven years for some regulatory records. Is Redwood able to support long-term retention? Cost is a factor.
[04:25] Jia: For long-term retention we recommend exporting logs to customer-owned storage (S3 Glacier or equivalent); Redwood can export via a scheduled export job. For hosted customers we'll help automate that export but the storage costs would be on Bluemoor. For Dedicated/Private you fully control retention policies.
[04:39] Rajiv: What about redaction — our logs contain PII in some fields. Can Redwood support automatic redaction at ingest?
[04:46] Jia: We offer configurable field redaction at ingest and policies to hash or redact certain attributes. There's a tradeoff with debugging and quality telemetry, so we usually enable strict redaction for regulated streams and a separate sanitized telemetry stream for ops.
[04:58] Lena: Do you save full request payloads by default? We don't want full payload stored.
[05:03] Jia: By default we do not store full request payloads. We store metadata and small traces; full payloads are only stored if debug modes are enabled or if you opt in. For the pilot we can ensure debug is off and redaction is enforced.
[05:14] Tom: For SOC 2 evidence we will need a lifecycle for user access reviews and RBAC attestations. Does Redwood provide a built-in user access report?
[05:22] Jia: Yes, we provide periodic user access exports and change logs for admin actions. Those can be scheduled and we can also push snapshots to your S3 for archival.
[05:32] Maya: Just to interject — customers have used that export during SOC audits and it's been acceptable as evidence as long as it includes timestamps, actor IDs and action details.
[05:41] Rajiv: Are there any caveats for model caching and KV cache related to residency? We use KV cache for latency.
[05:48] Jia: Good point. KV cache is location-dependent — for hosted we place caches in-region. For Private deployments it's entirely within your network. We do not shard KV to other regions unless configured for multi-region replication which you can opt out of.
[06:02] Tom: Can we get a written data flow that includes where caches are persisted, where logs are buffered, and any third-party telemetry?
[06:09] Jia: Yes, I'll include the data flow diagram in the packet I send.
[06:14] Lena: For ISO 27001, we'd like to see the scope statement and the Statement of Applicability at a high level.
[06:20] Samir: We can share the ISO scope summary and an SoA redacted version. The Trust Center PDF has the SoA and the control mapping. We'll gate access via NDA if necessary.
[06:30] Sofia: Our legal team will want the encryption-at-rest and in-transit specifics — TLS versions, cipher suites, and FIPS mode availability.
[06:37] Jia: We use TLS 1.2 and 1.3, with modern ciphers; FIPS endpoints are available for dedicated/private as needed. For in-transit we can provide cipher lists and cert rotation cadence. For at-rest, encryption is AES-256 and can be KMS-backed.
[06:50] Tom: One more — what about key rotation? We need annual rotation and immediate revocation workflow.
[06:56] Jia: Our recommended policy is quarterly rotation for wrapping keys and periodic rotation of data keys as you need. For revocation, we provide key policy updates and can trigger a soft-fail over to a fallback key while you investigate. For Private deployments the revocation is under customer KMS control.
[07:10] Rajiv: Any compliance limitations we should know about if we start with hosted and move to dedicated later?
[07:16] Samir: The main consideration is the timing and data migration path. Hosted is quicker to get started but for the tightest control (KMS/HSM and full log ownership) Dedicated/Private is recommended. We have migration guides and can help export and import model weights and telemetry.
[07:30] Tom: Ok, let's agree on next steps and deliverables.
[07:33] Samir: Recap: Redwood will send redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary, Jia will send KMS flow and dataflow diagrams, and we'll schedule a follow-up technical pilot call to validate EU region routing and run a small benchmark. Bluemoor will confirm contractual residency constraints and list of controls for pilot.
[07:51] Lena: Sounds good. We'll also prepare a list of internal stakeholders for the pilot — security, infra, and compliance.
[07:58] Maya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot and include the materials when Samir and Jia send them.
[08:05] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[08:07] Samir: Thank you all — we'll action the items and be in touch.

End of transcript.
